arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Justice Gorsuch asked which of three argument categories remained preserved after the district court's order.
Justice Gorsuch noted that some purely legal questions might not require renewal, but disputed facts remained.
Justice Gorsuch asked if the side that brought the case was abandoning fact-bound arguments about procedural opacity and frustration.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of appellate review after a district court denies summary judgment. The core conflict centers on whether purely legal issues remain live for appeal when a court declines to resolve them at the pretrial stage.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on April 24, 2023.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to confirm that purely legal issues denied at summary judgment remain preserved for appellate review.
the opposing side wants the Court to hold that denying summary judgment leaves claims and defenses live until trial.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that resolving a purely legal issue against a party at summary judgment preserves that issue for appeal.
the opposing side argues that denying summary judgment delays final adjudication of a claim or defense until trial, keeping it live.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Jackson asked why the district judge's order did not need to resolve disputes about Younger's adherence to process.
Justice Thomas questioned whether the practice defies standard procedures when parties try cases differently than anticipated at pretrial stages.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute determines how appellate courts review lower-court denials of summary judgment. It clarifies which legal issues survive pretrial motions. The outcome shapes the finality of district court orders. It affects the efficiency of the federal judicial process. It defines the boundary between pretrial and trial-stage adjudication.
